edits.previous: A Lean `Fin n` parameter or result is an `Integer`, the same as `Nat`. For `Library.mirror (value : Fin 10) : Fin 10`, `mirror(3)` returns `6`. `mirror(10)` raises `RangeError` with the message `arg0 is not below its Fin 10 bound`. A negative value raises the `RangeError` that `Nat` raises, and a non-Integer raises `TypeError`. The package checks the bound before it calls Lean, so caller data is unchanged and a later valid call still works. `Fin 0` parameters reject every value, and bounds wider than 64 bits are compared exactly. A comment on each generated method and the gem README state the bound. Top-level parameters and results are supported, including inside `Array`, `List` and `Option` (for example `Array (Fin 10)` or `Option (List (Fin 10))`): every element is checked before Lean is called, an empty array or `none` is valid even for `Fin 0`, and a rejection names the parameter and the bound of the element that failed. Fields, callbacks, products and results are not; see the [installed checks](../evidence/native-fin-hosts-20261006.md) and the [container checks](../evidence/native-fin-containers-20261006.md).
